# Dhammahadayavibhaṅga (Vb 18)

**ID:** Vb 18
**Section:** Vibhaṅga (vb)

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Dhammahadayavibhaṅga* ("Analysis of the Heart of the Dhamma") is the eighteenth and concluding chapter of the *Vibhaṅga*, the second book of the Theravāda Abhidhamma Piṭaka (PTS Vibh 401–436) [von Hinüber 1996; SuttaCentral]. The figurative term *hadaya* ("heart") in its title denotes the "essence," "gist," or "summary" of the teachings, parallel to the usage in later Buddhist Sanskrit texts such as the *Prajñāpāramitāhṛdaya* [Nyanatiloka 1938/1957/2007]. Hajime Nakamura notes that this final chapter is considered a later addition to the work [Nakamura 1980]. The text possesses an independent *mātikā* (matrix) and proceeds primarily as a catechism of questions and answers structuring twelve core doctrinal categories, including aggregates (*khandha*), nutriments (*āhāra*), and root causes (*hetu*) [von Hinüber 1996; Nyanatiloka 1938/1957/2007]. It also provides detailed enumerations concerning cosmology and the realms of existence, notably the life-spans of diverse classes of devas, for which reason it was later drawn upon in post-canonical thematic anthologies treating heavenly rebirth (*sagga*) [Norman 1983]. According to the *Aṭṭhasālinī*, a sectarian group known as the Vitaṇḍavādins rejected the canonical status of the *Kathāvatthu* and replaced it in their Abhidhamma basket with a work called the *Mahādhammahadaya*, which traditional commentators and modern scholars identify as being closely related or essentially identical in substance to this chapter [Nyanatiloka 1938/1957/2007; von Hinüber 1996]. Commentaries on the *Gulissānisutta* indicate that forest-dwelling monks were expected to master this text alongside the fundamental Abhidhamma mātikās [Patt 1993]. Its primary commentary forms part of the *Pañcappakaraṇa-aṭṭhakathā* [von Hinüber 1996].

Curated cross-references noted on SuttaCentral link the chapter to topics in the *Saṅgīti Sutta* (DN 33), the *Dhammasaṅgaṇī*, *Yamaka*, *Puggalapaññatti*, and other Vibhaṅga treatises [SuttaCentral]. DharmaNexus detects dense internal text reuse between the *Dhammahadayavibhaṅga* and other Abhidhamma treatises, prominently the *Abhidhammamātikā*, the *Khandhavibhaṅga*, the *Dhātuvibhaṅga*, and multiple sections of the *Paṭṭhāna*, as well as commentarial cross-citations in the *Pañcapakaraṇa-aṭṭhakathā* and *Vibhaṅga-mūlaṭīkā* [DharmaNexus]. Outside Pali, DharmaNexus identifies textual correspondences with Sanskrit and Tibetan scholastic compendia, including the *Arthaviniścayasūtra*, Nāgārjuna's *Dharmasaṃgraha*, the *Śrāvakabhūmi*, and notably the *Āyuḥparyantasūtra* (reflecting its cosmographical accounts of deva lifespans) [DharmaNexus].
